stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current models being restricted to a single robot embodiment, enabling learning from diverse, internet-scale video data.
Aims to create zero-shot physical simulators by leveraging heterogeneous video data from human and robotic agents to learn generalizable physics.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speedup for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon using MLX.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA has introduced Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated support for MLX.
This integration enables faster performance when running Ollama specifically on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries (AI Overviews) on search results pages.
This expansion pushes traditional organic search links further down the results page.
The change represents a continued integration and prioritization of generative AI within Google's core search experience.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's blacklisting of Anthropic was illegal.
Anthropic's refusal to support lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance is a key factor in the story.
The ruling highlights legal challenges against government actions targeting AI companies based on their ethical stances.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have arrested two individuals linked to the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP is known for conducting extensive and persistent cyberattacks.
The group successfully infected over 1,000 organizations through a supply-chain attack campaign.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in product execution harnesses, where harmful tool use is a greater threat than simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current automated red-teaming, specifically the risk of retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack methods.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by providing a realistic testing environment that avoids the privacy issues of internal corporate data.
Evaluates LLMs across multiple tasks using a corpus exceeding 230,000 documents, focusing on complex, real-world information retrieval.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA) to adapt advertising for Generative AI.
Shifts advertising from predefined slots to a token-level mechanism embedded within the generation process.
Advertisers influence the model by reporting local continuation values to induce specific next-token policies.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon.
This allows support for a greater variety of models across a broader range of hardware.

stories.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Sophisticated generative AI tools are flooding the internet with music mimicking human artists.
The core issue is the unauthorized algorithmic derivation of melodies and vocals from existing artists' work.
The problem is complicated by some creators openly admitting AI use while others deny it.

stories.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma redefined 'Project Helix' from a singular next-gen console to a 'family of devices'.
The announcement suggests Microsoft is pursuing a multi-device ecosystem rather than a single hardware iteration.
This shift indicates a potential strategic move toward broader platform integration for future Xbox hardware.

stories.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The EPA is planning to remove a federal rule requiring public notice for certain industrial sites.
This change specifically impacts data centers, allowing them potentially to hide air pollution.
The move comes amid increasing community backlash against the environmental impact of new data centers.

stories.title: DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia’s AI effects on everything
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: An unofficial version of Nvidia's DLSS 5 has been leaked and is being utilized by modders.
The leaked code was reportedly found within an early-access build of NBA 2K27.
Modders are applying this AI upscaling technology to popular titles like Skyrim, Cyberpunk 2077, and GTA V.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: The article investigates the practical difficulties users face when exercising their data privacy rights.
A survey of 100 companies revealed that privacy requests frequently result in confusion or failure to comply.
This highlights systemic issues in how large organizations manage and respond to data deletion and access requests.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has implemented a safety feature in its AI glasses to prevent unauthorized recording.
The glasses will cease recording if the user covers the designated safety light.
This update addresses privacy concerns related to nonconsensual recording capabilities of the hardware.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge derived from AI agent experiences.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and reuse learned skills across different interaction iterations.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM software debugging by criticizing the reliance on large-scale, successful agent trajectory datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT).
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision when used directly.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance on real-world software issues by refining the supervision signal beyond mere task success.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Traditional code review is an iterative, multi-round process, which current LLM-based tools often oversimplify into a single, static decision.
The paper introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark real-world code review, addressing the limitations of static evaluation methods.
The research aims to capture the complex, interactive problem-solving inherent in realistic software development review cycles.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions using discrete flow matching.
The approach models reactions not as molecular topology edits or molecule generation, but as transformations in electron occupation vectors.
This represents a shift toward a more fundamental, mechanistic understanding of chemical reactions using AI.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES) as an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining traceable, auditable execution.
Achieves separation by placing persona in one trust domain and execution in another, connected by a governed contract bridge.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in current AI model security scanner evaluations, which often only measure successful judgments.
It introduces a controlled, artifact-backed benchmark using a synthetic corpus of 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts.
The research evaluates existing scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, Fickling) against a dataset with binary security ground truth.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The study addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed sepsis severity indices by proposing a new, learned approach.
It utilized a retrospective, two-site study involving over 36,800 adult patients meeting Sepsis-3 criteria.
The core innovation is developing a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories without requiring hour-by-hour supervision.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map these moral foundations geometrically.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-weight sepsis severity indices.
A novel machine learning model was developed to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The study utilized a large, retrospective dataset from two different hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map the geometric relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for academia and open-source communities.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a model trained using a single RTX 5090 GPU, aiming for cost-efficiency.
Highlights the need for accessible, hardware-friendly, and open-source training recipes, contrasting with the multi-million dollar costs of training larger models.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It systematically analyzes ES dynamics to compare its performance against established methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates that ES offers a performance advantage over GRPO in certain reasoning tasks.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) used to boost LLM performance.
Leverages the insight that LLM failure modes follow structured patterns across different model scales within the same family.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories, hindering systematic reuse.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by making learned skills reusable resources.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM training for software engineering: relying solely on successful agent trajectories for fine-tuning.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain inefficient, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance by mitigating the negative impact of noisy supervision during fine-tuning.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM post-training methods (like RL and OPSD) which require ground-truth labels.
It proposes Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO) as an alternative to traditional ground-truth reliance.
TTPO mitigates the fragility of using pseudo-labels by observing and addressing asymmetric failure modes during rollouts.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM-based code review, which treats the process as a single, static decision.
It proposes MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a more realistic, multi-round, and interactive manner.
The research aims to improve the accuracy and applicability of LLMs in capturing the complex, iterative nature of real-world software development.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a known issue in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrowed reasoning.
The proposed solution introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain generative diversity during RLVR training.
The work aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities while mitigating the degradation in performance (pass@$k$) caused by overly constrained policies.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study uses six independent linear probes, one for each category of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT), to test model understanding.
The core question is whether LLMs can geometrically distinguish and map the relationships between different moral foundations.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Clinical language models suffer from poor generalization due to reliance on note-specific artifacts (e.g., templates, boilerplate).
The proposed CAST framework uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAE) to identify and suppress these artifacts in clinical text classification.
CAST aims to create auditable models by exposing human-interpretable features from Transformer activations.
